findings.evidence: Gotcha "Softening a deadline into \"when you get a chance\" removes it: keep the date, soften only the framing." repeats NEVER line 58 "Polish away an explicit safety, escalation or deadline concern for friendliness; soften the delivery, keep the flag."
findings.fix: Delete the deadline Gotcha. Use the space for a channel-specific fact that the model would not infer, for example that a Slack thread reply without 'also send to channel' is never seen by people outside the thread.

findings.evidence: Generic checklist: "ask in the first two lines, one request per message, observable behaviour only, deadline or owner stated, register matches the reader" is generic writing advice the model already knows
findings.fix: Keep the fallback but reduce it to a pointer: 'offer the professional-communication checklist, headed "Generic checklist (no draft reviewed)"'. The preloaded skill already holds these rules.

findings.evidence: "For an outline: check that the opening names the audience's decision, order follows their need, and the close states the ask." The description promises architecture-review presentations, but this is the only outline guidance and it has no expert frame
findings.fix: Add a thinking step for presentations: 'Before reviewing an architecture-review outline, ask: which decision or objection will the senior reader raise first, and is the trade-off or alternative shown before the recommendation?' Then list the risk-category items specific to outlines, such as a missing rollback or cost slide.

findings.evidence: "Send anything, edit the user's files, or reach external systems. You are read-only." gives no non-obvious reason, and the tools allowlist already enforces it
findings.fix: Replace it with an anti-pattern that has a reason, for example: 'NEVER play the counterpart as instantly persuaded: an easy rehearsal gives false confidence for the real conversation.'

findings.evidence: "Done when the template below holds the requested analysis" makes the full five-part Review Summary mandatory even for a one-line Slack message
findings.fix: Add a default with an escape hatch: 'For a draft of two lines or fewer, give only Biggest risk and one Current -> Suggested line; use the full template otherwise.'

findings.evidence: Intake line 18 routes "upcoming conversation, no draft -> Roleplay", but Handoffs says "when the user wants to deliver feedback, outline the SBI parts from their facts, ask them to write the message, and review it as a draft". With feedback to deliver and no draft, the two branches conflict
findings.fix: Add a rule to Intake step 1: 'Feedback to deliver with no draft: if it will be written, outline the SBI parts and ask for a draft (Review); if it will be spoken, outline the SBI parts, then Roleplay.'

findings.evidence: "Done after the agreed number of exchanges (default three)". No intake step ever asks for or agrees the number of exchanges
findings.fix: In Intake step 2, add: 'For Roleplay, use three exchanges unless the user names a number.'
